approved_review_contexts.checked_scope: The exact waiting-list state exposes only mutually eligible untried colleges to an active applicant. Every new application satisfies the two-sided sign test, and the terminal stability and applicant-optimality results require only the strict-list domain; they have no global applicant-positive-implies-college-positive premise.
approved_review_contexts.formal_meaning: An applicant-college pair is eligible for the Section 4 procedure exactly when the applicant lists the college as acceptable and the college has not eliminated the applicant as unacceptable. In the numerical representation this is the pairwise conjunction of a positive applicant score and a positive college score.
approved_review_contexts.why_needed: The source separately permits applicants to omit colleges they would never attend and forbids applications to colleges that would never admit the applicant. This is a filter on each possible application, not a global assumption that every college acceptable to an applicant must accept that applicant. Recording the pairwise rule prevents the earlier global implication from being smuggled into Theorem 2.

approved_review_contexts.checked_scope: Theorem 1 uses the positive complete-list encoding. The displayed college definitions and Theorem 2 use the incomplete-list encoding with zero as unmatched. The direct Section 4 runner filters to mutually positive pairs before choosing an application, and completed stability excludes assignment to a negative pair, so no paper-facing conclusion assigns source meaning to the relative order among omitted alternatives.
approved_review_contexts.formal_meaning: Lean represents each finite strict preference list by a nonzero injective real-valued score with zero as the outside option. In the complete marriage model every opposite-side participant is acceptable and receives a positive score. In the college model a positive score means listed and acceptable, while omitted alternatives receive arbitrary distinct negative scores solely to make the numerical function total.
approved_review_contexts.why_needed: The source uses finite ordered lists, including incomplete lists in the college model, whereas the reusable matching API takes total real-valued functions. The sign convention preserves acceptability and the score order preserves every listed ranking; making the arbitrary order among omitted negative alternatives explicit prevents that Lean-only totalization from being mistaken for additional source preference data.
